portal_hypertension.abstract: Portal hypertension is the principal driver of decompensation in advanced chronic liver disease, yet in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) it deviates from the classical sinusoidal paradigm. Growing evidence points to a mixed sinusoidal-presinusoidal phenotype in which the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) may underestimate true portal pressure, and in which decompensation and varices can occur at lower HVPG values than in viral cirrhosis. portal_hypertension.abstract: The applicability of non-invasive tests (NITs) for clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is controversial. We performed a head-to-head comparison of various NITs for CSPH and evaluated rule-in/-out criteria. We conducted a retrospective study including 283 patients with HCC undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement at the Vienna Hepatic Haemodynamic Lab with available, same-day data on NITs (i.e., liver stiffness measurement [LSM], platelet count [PLT], von Willebrand factor antigen [VWF:Ag], and the ratio of VWF:Ag and PLT [VITRO]). portal_hypertension.abstract: Portal hypertension is a major determinant of disease progression and clinical outcomes in cirrhosis. The Baveno consensus has progressively moved its focus from the treatment of established complications towards earlier risk stratification, prevention of decompensation and modification of the natural history of the disease. Baveno VIII consolidates and extends this approach across the different stages of advanced chronic liver disease.
